identity.name: Byelorussian Soviet Socialist Republic
native_names: Беларуская Савецкая Сацыялістычная Рэспубліка (Biełaruskaja Saviecka Sacyjalistyčnaja Respublika)

land.text: Cliopatria draws Belarus inside its Russian Republic shapes

predecessors.note: Proclaimed at Smolensk on 31 December 1918 from the Belarusian lands of the former empire.

successors.note: Independence declared 25 August 1991, renamed the Republic of Belarus 19 September 1991.

capitals.name: Smolensk
capitals.note: Proclaimed at Smolensk on 1 January 1919 (the page: the conference met on 30-31 December 1918 and 'The next day' the republic was proclaimed); the seat moved to Minsk on 7 January 1919.

capitals.name: Minsk
capitals.note: Minsk from 7 January 1919; evacuated to Smolensk on 8 August 1919 when the Poles took Minsk and re-established in Minsk on 31 July 1920.

correction.text: the Minsk lands, the core of the republic

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 45,522 km2: the Minsk lands as the core. The page gives 52,400 km2 for the republic left after the Treaty of Riga; Minsk Oblast with the capital is 45,522 km2 (ratio 1.15); the page names no districts. In 1919-1920 Polish forces held Minsk from 8 August 1919 to the Red Army's return (re-established in Minsk 31 July 1920).

region.text: proclaimed at Smolensk, seated at Minsk

ledger.note: 1919, 1 January: the Byelorussian Soviet republic is proclaimed in Smolensk ("The next day" after the conference of 30-31 December 1918); the seat moves to Minsk on 7 January 1919. The page names the cities, not a boundary; the Minsk lands are the researcher's reading.
1919, 7 January: the seat moves from Smolensk to Minsk.
1919, 30 January: renamed the Soviet Socialist Republic of Byelorussia (SSRB) after separation from the Russian SFSR.

region.text: the Minsk lands, the core of the republic

ledger.note: 1919, 28 February: the Bolsheviks decide to merge the Lithuanian and Byelorussian republics into the Lithuanian-Belorussian SSR (Litbel); the Vitebsk and Mogilev governorates are transferred to the RSFSR and the Gomel Governorate is created on 26 April.

region.text: the Vitebsk and Mogilev lands returned by Russia in March 1924

ledger.note: 1919, February-April: the Vitebsk and Mogilev governorates pass to the RSFSR (the page ties the transfer to the Litbel decision of 28 February; no day).

region.text: the Minsk lands, the core of the republic

ledger.note: 1919, 8 August: Polish forces capture Minsk and the capital is evacuated to Smolensk the same day.

region.text: the Minsk lands, the core of the republic

ledger.note: 1919, 8 August: Minsk falls to Poland in the Polish-Soviet War.

region.text: the Minsk lands, the core of the republic

ledger.note: 1920, 31 July: the republic is re-established in Minsk (the page gives the date, not the military operation).

region.text: the Minsk lands, the core of the republic

ledger.note: 1921, 18 March: the Treaty of Riga ends the Polish-Soviet War; Poland recognises Soviet Belarus, withdraws from "areas further east, notably Minsk" and keeps western Belarus; the republic left is 52,400 km2 (the BSSR page dates the treaty February 1921).
1922, 30 December: the Byelorussian republic signs the Treaty on the Creation of the USSR with the Russian, Ukrainian and Transcaucasian republics and becomes a constituent republic of the Union.

region.text: the Vitebsk and Mogilev lands returned by Russia in March 1924

ledger.note: 1924, March: Russia returns most of the Vitebsk and Mogilev governorates and parts of Smolensk to the republic, doubling it to 110,600 km2.

region.text: Gomel and Rechytsa, added 6 December 1926 (about 15,700 km2)

ledger.note: 1926, 6 December: parts of the RSFSR's Gomel Governorate, including Gomel and Rechytsa, are added; the area rises to 126,300 km2.
1939, 17 September: the Soviet Union invades Poland from the east.
1939, 28 September: the German-Soviet demarcation treaty gives the Soviet Union "almost all Polish territory east of the line of the rivers Pisa, Narew, Western Bug and San".

1939, 15 November (infobox; the Soviet occupation began in September): the former Polish territories are "incorporated into the Belarusian SSR", except Vilnius and its surroundings, which go to Lithuania.

region.text: Belarus within the borders of 1939-1991 (the Bialystok area is not drawn)

ledger.note: 1941, summer: "Belarus was occupied by Nazi Germany"; much of the territory becomes the General District Belarus within Reichskommissariat Ostland.

region.text: Belarus within the borders of 1939-1991 (the Bialystok area is not drawn)

ledger.note: 1944: the German occupation ends. Bridging: the page gives no liberation date; the year is the researcher's judgement, and the page does not mention the return of the Bialystok area to Poland.

region.text: Belarus within the borders of 1939-1991 (the Bialystok area is not drawn)

ledger.note: 1991, 25 August: Belarus declares independence (the republic is renamed the Republic of Belarus on 19 September 1991; sovereignty had been declared on 27 July 1990).

wars.name: Polish-Soviet War

zones.text: the Minsk lands, the core of the republic

wars.outcome: Poland takes Minsk on 8 August 1919; the Red Army re-establishes the republic in Minsk on 31 July 1920; Treaty of Riga (18 March 1921) leaves western Belarus with Poland.

wars.name: Soviet invasion of Poland
wars.note: Ordered 17 September, treaty of demarcation 28 September 1939.

certainty.note: Civil and Polish-Soviet war front; the republic held cities.
The Riga line (1921), the 1924 and 1926 transfers, and the 1939 demarcation are dated lines.

sources.title: Byelorussian Soviet Socialist Republic
sources.note: Infobox (31 December 1918, 7 January, 30 January and 28 February 1919, 31 July 1920, 30 December 1922, 25 August 1991, 207,600 km2), 52,400 / 110,600 / 126,300 km2, 1924, 1926 and 1939 changes, German occupation.

sources.title: Treaty of Riga
sources.note: Signed 18 March 1921; Poland recognises Soviet Belarus; Minsk stays Soviet.

notes: No Cliopatria row; Belarus is drawn inside the Russian Republic, Republics of the Soviet Union and USSR shapes (and the Polish rows for the west). The BSSR page dates the Treaty of Riga February 1921 (the Riga page: 18 March); the infobox proclamation 31 December 1918 (not 1 January 1919); Litbel 28 February (not 27). Not on the page: the dates of the liberation of Minsk (1944), the return of the Bialystok area to Poland in 1945, the Vilnius region's status in 1945, and the Polish-Soviet frontier of 1945. The 1919-1920 front is not detailed. Counterparts: second-polish-republic (eu-21) and nazi-germany exist; Lithuanian Soviet Socialist Republic / Litbel has no dossier.
